The arrangement is governed by two agreements between SWDD and IRSC: the Wastewater Treatment Agreement dated July 13, 2021, as amended December 14, 2021 (Amendment No. 1) and April 18, 2023 (Amendment No. 2) (the WTA), and the First Amended and Restated Site Access Agreement dated April 18, 2023 (the Site Access Agreement). item.description: The proposed LDR amendments being presented for the BCC’s consideration address Chapter 913, Subdivisions and Plats, and are intended to update the County’s subdivision and plat review and approval procedures to reflect changes to Chapter 177, Florida Statutes, particularly Sections 177.071 and 177.073. Section 177.071, Florida Statutes, requires qualifying plats and replats to be approved administratively rather than through an additional approval action by the local governing body. item.title: Indian River · 2026-12-01 · Board of County Commissioners Meeting (Board of County Commissioners): Fire Apparatus Potential Class Action Lawsuit
item.description: Indian River County has been contacted by attorneys representing other counties, municipalities, and purchasers of fire apparatus regarding a pending class action lawsuit filed against 4 large emergency equipment manufacturers. The suit alleges that the four companies have engaged in anti-competitive practices resulting in extremely high prices and low supply. This has occurred through a series of mergers and acquisitions that have shrunk the entire market significantly. Additionally, the suit claims that due to these illegal business activities costs of parts and repairs have been affected as well. item.description: The Lakeside West P.D. final plat consists of 201 single-family residential lots on 126.70 acres, resulting in a density of 1.58 units per acre. item.description: The Windsor North Village P.D. final plat consists of 40 single-family residential lots and two future townhouse development tracts that will consist of 6 multi-family units, resulting in 46 units overall within the planned development. The project is on 52.96 acres, resulting in a density of .87 units per acre. The site is located between Highway AlA and Jungle Trail, immediately north of the existing Windsor PD development. The subject site is zoned PD, Planned Development, and has L-1, Low-Density Residential-1 (up to 3 units/acre), future land use designation.

item.description: On May 17, 2022, the Board adopted Ordinance No. 2022-007, amending the Children’s Services Advisory Committee (CSAC) provisions of Chapter 103 of the County Code. item.description: Gifford Dock Park is located at the east end of Gifford Dock Road (also referred to as 45th Street). The park has been a historic feature of the Gifford community for many generations. The park contains an unimproved parking area and a pier that requires significant renovation. The County recently approved a funding MOU with the City of Vero Beach to provide a shaded pavilion within the park boundaries. To the south of Gifford Dock Park the County recently acquired 15.47 acres of conservation land through the 2022 voter-approved Environmental Land Acquisition Bond process. This acquisition was referred to as the “Osprey Estates” project. This Lagoon front property is dominated by mangroves that were once managed for mosquito control. item.description: Since the completion of the 700MHz radio system project, Communications International, Inc. ("Ci"), the factory certified regional service partner of the manufacturer, has provided the daily maintenance for the radio system. To guarantee continuity of essential services, the County requires Ci to have certified service technicians available twenty-four (24) hours a day for immediate repairs. Ci is the only regional vendor qualified to perform the maintenance and repairs, and has been designated as the sole source provider by the Board since March 1, 2011, and most recently renewed on August 4, 2026.

item.description: The Wabasso Island community consists of approximately 110 homes on septic tanks adjacent to the Indian River Lagoon. The proposed project comprises upgrades of approximately 2300 linear feet (LF) of a 4-inch water main and approximately 2100 LF of a 3-inch sewer main on Live Oak Drive, and the extension of approximately 13,500 linear feet of public sewer infrastructure that consists of new sewer mains and laterals to connect the properties. It is estimated that the septic to sewer conversions will result in approximately 3,600 lbs. per year of nitrogen reduction.

item.description: Floravon Shores is a subdivision of 19 properties on septic systems, adjacent to the Indian River Lagoon (IRL), in North Indian River County. The septic tanks in this area potentially leach harmful nutrients into groundwater that leads to the IRL. The Floravon Shores Septic-to-Sewer (S2S) Project, IRCDUS Project ID 21.19.556, will construct approximately 1,300 linear feet of public gravity sewer infrastructure that consists of new sewer mains and laterals to connect the homes. An initial bid (2025045) was initially awarded on April 6, 2026, but due to a three month delay in the award process, the Contractor ultimately determined they could no longer honor their October 8, 2025 price ($896,900), and the Board subsequently terminated the award and authorized Staff to rebid the project.

These public gatherings can attract large crowds, which is a target for hostile action-based mass casualty incidents. The Meridian Archer Trailer Kit 1000 is a protection system which reduces an assailant’s capability to weaponize a vehicle in targeted pedestrian areas. The kit’s included equipment list is attached to this Agenda Item for review. The Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM) has offered a Meridian Archer Trailer Kit 1000 to the County through a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA). item.title: Indian River · 2026-10-20 · Board of County Commissioners Meeting (Board of County Commissioners): Gifford Dock Interlocal Agreement with the City of Vero Beach
item.description: The County and the City of Vero Beach recently worked together on a project in which the County granted a utility easement for the installation of a reclaimed water pipeline at Gifford Dock Park. In exchange for the utility easement, the City offered to pay $50,000 towards the construction of a pavilion at the park. This Interlocal Agreement is the codification of the discussions and will assist with the construction of the pavilion while other improvements are also being completed.

item.description: The Hobart Scrub property is a Tier One ELAP parcel located at 4525 77th Street that has been approved by the Board for negotiation of a possible purchase. The property is approximately 161.87+/- acres and abut the railroad tracks to the East and Sandridge to the West. Indian River · 2026-10-20 · Board of County Commissioners Meeting (Board of County Commissioners): Request Approval to Submit Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission Derelict Vessel Grant Applications for the 2026-2027 Fiscal Year
item.description: The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) authorizes the removal of derelict vessels from the Indian River Lagoon and St. Sebastian River within Indian River County. Law enforcement officers investigate and determine vessel status under Florida Statutes 705.101 (3) and 823.11. Once authorized, vessels may be removed and properly disposed of to eliminate hazards to navigation and the environment. FWC makes available two 100% reimbursement grants to support removal efforts: the Bulk Derelict Vessel Removal Grant and a Rapid Removal Grant. Applications are submitted to the FWC Boating and Waterways Law Enforcement Division. If funding is available, recipients are notified and grant documents are provided for execution.

item.title: Indian River · 2026-10-06 · Board of County Commissioners Meeting (Board of County Commissioners): Approval of Public Medical Transportation Letter of Agreement between Indian River County Emergency Services District and the Agency for Health Care Administration (Year Eight)
item.description: Staff seeks consideration and approval of a revised Letter of Agreement (LOA) with the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) for the receipt of Public Emergency Medical Transportation–Managed Care Organization (PEMT MCO) payments to Indian River County for the current fiscal year. Due to delays by AHCA in providing the required agreement documentation, the finalized information was not received in time for presentation prior to the October 1 deadline. To meet the submission requirement, staff provided a placeholder LOA reflecting an amount of $1.00 until AHCA supplied the actual agreement amount. The correct dollar amount of $933,953.33 has now been provided and is submitted herewith for approval.
